first.rationale: Current situation shows activation down 6% and onboarding completion down 4% QoQ. Memory_91 demonstrated that activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged accounts to first meaningful action—this directly addresses the activation decline. Memory_86 showed that simplified onboarding lifted early adoption, but since onboarding completion is only down 4% versus activation down 6%, the steeper drop suggests engagement post-signup is the primary lever. Activation messaging is lower-risk than promotional pricing (memory_73 shows retention harm) and more immediate than referral incentives (memory_57, better for established customers). Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is valuable but won't help self-serve SMB accounts losing share to competitor pricing. Verifying memories_86 and memory_91 will confirm whether in-product messaging can be deployed quickly and whether the previous uplift conditions still apply. A standard_experiment scale allows measured rollout while preserving the ability to course-correct if competitive pricing pressures require a secondary response.

mid.rationale: Archive verification confirms both memories. exp_86 showed +13% completion and +3% retention uplift; exp_91 showed +6% activation and +1% retention uplift with +11% week-one engagement. Current state: activation down 6% QoQ, onboarding completion down 4% QoQ. Activation messaging directly reversed a 6% deficit in the prior experiment, making it the most targeted response to the immediate decline. The +1% retention from exp_91 is conservative relative to risk, and the engagement uplift is measurable without the retention harm seen in promotional_pricing (memory_73). Competitor entry pricing pressure on SMB segments argues against promotional_pricing response—it would erode margins and retention further. Referral_incentive (memory_57) works best on established customers, not the activation-constrained base. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) helps pipeline quality but doesn't solve self-serve SMB activation leakage. Standard_experiment scale allows validated learning while preserving resource for follow-up if needed. Activation messaging preserves uncertainty by testing one lever at a time rather than bundling with onboarding changes; if this underperforms, onboarding simplification remains a secondary option.

final2.rationale: Competitive pressure has intensified with doubled churn conversations among price-sensitive SMB accounts. However, committing to promotional_pricing now carries elevated risk: memory_73 explicitly warns that targeted promotional pricing 'materially reduced 30-day retention' and should not be generalized as a growth strategy. Under current churn pressure, retention harm would compound the problem. Activation_messaging remains the highest-confidence lever with confirmed +6% activation and +11% week-one engagement (exp_91), addressing the root activation decline (down 6% QoQ) that likely underlies some churn susceptibility. Stronger engagement and faster time-to-value may retain price-sensitive accounts better than discounting. A standard_experiment maintains speed while preserving flexibility: if activation messaging shows rapid traction, it buys time to evaluate pricing response with better data next week. If it underperforms, the verification budget will refresh and allow memory_73 to be re-examined under clearer conditions. Enterprise_sales_assist and referral_incentive do not address immediate SMB churn. Simplify_onboarding is secondary (4% completion decline vs 6% activation decline). The downstream_value_risk is flagged because price competition may ultimately require pricing response, but deploying it before testing engagement leverage risks unnecessary margin erosion and retention damage.
